name: boarding-pass
title: Boarding Pass
description: A paper boarding pass with real notches: tap the barcode to scan it and the stub tears off with a stamp.

perf.budget: The ticket shape is built once per size; the band slides in on arrival and the scan runs one UI-thread timing and spring. Nothing animates at rest.

measurements.notes: Measured during scans (scanner line with a blurred glow, then the stub tearing). Frame stats put app work at about 2 ms and render-thread work at 1 ms a frame; the rest is the emulator waiting on its virtual GPU.

a11y.reducedMotion: The pass appears in place and a scan tears and stamps the stub at once, with no scanner line.
a11y.screenReader: The pass reads as one summary (route, times, passenger, gate and seat); the barcode is a button that becomes "Boarded".
a11y.touchTarget: The whole stub, 112 pt tall, is the scan button.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { BoardingPass } from '@/components/kinetik/boarding-pass';

<BoardingPass
  airline="Northwind"
  flight="KN 1321"
  cabin="Premium"
  booking="AG7890"
  from={{ code: 'CDG', city: 'Paris', time: '14:30' }}
  to={{ code: 'JFK', city: 'New York', time: '17:45' }}
  duration="8h 15m"
  passenger="Olivia Bennett"
  details={[
    { label: 'Gate', value: 'B12' },
    { label: 'Seat', value: '12A' },
  ]}
  onScan={checkIn}
/>;
```

## When to use

- Showing a ticket, pass or booking that the user presents or checks in with.

## When not to use

- As a real scannable code: the barcode is a decorative pattern. Render a real barcode or QR code for gates.

## Notes

- The notches are cut out of the ticket shape, so the pass sits on any background.
- The pass is paper-white on both themes. `accent` colours the striped band.
- Without `onScan` the stub is not a button. `boarded` starts the pass already torn and stamped.
- `barcodeBars(code)` is exported: the same code always draws the same pattern.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add boarding-pass`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
